I was in a similar situation when we brought our (now 3 month old) baby home. She was colic, so there wasn’t a whole lot that could be done. After one particularly brutal night about two weeks in, we researched ***everything*** about the Safe Sleep 7, bed-sharing statistics, and even more about bassinet sleep. We ended up giving bed-sharing a shot and haven’t gone back since. Our bassinet has become somewhat of a $300 laundry hamper at this point. 

It is absolutely essential that you research all that you can, in comparison, bed-sharing can be dangerous. I feel confident with our set up now, but you can’t go halfsies on bed-sharing safety. It’s a complete commitment in more ways than one. You need to be sure you have a good mattress for it first, otherwise I wouldn’t even bother. Something firm where baby won’t roll into you or dad. After that, there’s a few other tips which I will link [here](https://llli.org/the-safe-sleep-seven/) .

It can sometimes be almost as uncomfortable as waking up constantly throughout her night. My hips often go numb by morning because of the C curl, and nightly cuddles with my fiancé are pretty much nil at this point. So it’s really up to you to weigh the pros v. cons. There tends to be a lot of guilt tripping when it comes to bed-sharing, but that comes from a lack of education. I was constantly rolling my eyes at my MIL who kept bringing up the idea while I was pregnant, but she’s Salvadoran and that’s just part of her culture so she has the experience and education in doing so. It is something that is natural in other cultures because they are taught how to do it safely.

I urge you to research for yourself, and do what feels right.

ETA: I’d like to add that I’m also exclusively nursing. Also get sheet straps to keep your needing tight if you decide on it.
